results.title: 10 Reactive Resume Alternative Picks for 2026
results.content:
FlowCV and OpenResume are the direct free-first choices. FlowCV prioritizes free watermark-free PDF export and visual control. OpenResume prioritizes local browser storage, no sign-up, and a single-column layout. FlowCV gives more presentation flexibility. OpenResume gives a tighter privacy and simplicity story.

JSON Resume and Overleaf suit technical users who want deeper control. JSON Resume treats the resume as structured data that can live in Git and feed multiple renderers. Overleaf treats it as a typeset document with precise layout control. Both can produce excellent results, but both require more responsibility for setup, maintenance, and PDF testing. [...] Use JSON Resume when Git-based versioning, programmatic transformations, and themeable output are central requirements. It's the right tool for an engineer who wants resume-as-data. It's the wrong tool for someone who wants to write naturally and export a stable PDF with minimal setup.

## 6. Teal

Teal is an all-in-one job-search platform rather than a focused document editor. It combines an AI resume writer and rewriter with keyword matching, an ATS checker, job-description insights, a tracker, and outreach tooling. That makes it useful for engineers applying across many similar roles and needing help managing the surrounding process. [...] Teal, Resume.io, and Enhancv make more sense when tailoring guidance and broader job-search features justify paid access. Teal is strongest for tracking and job-description matching. Resume.io favors template breadth and guided creation. Enhancv supports richer storytelling and AI feedback, but visual layouts need stricter ATS checks.

Standard Resume is the speed choice for LinkedIn-based setup. It sacrifices Markdown and deep source portability for a quick path from an existing profile to a polished web resume and PDF.
